hero_sub: Baroque churches of pink stone, an aqueduct of 74 arches and vineyards in the hills, thirty-five minutes from Toluca and far from traffic.

story: Querétaro is two cities at once. The historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site of pink and ochre stone, baroque churches and quiet plazas, where the conspiracy that set off Mexico's War of Independence was planned in 1810. Its aqueduct, finished in 1735, still strides across the eastern side of town on 74 arches, the tallest close to 30 meters high, and at night the whole center glows under warm lights.

Around that old core, Querétaro has become one of Mexico's fastest-growing industrial and aerospace hubs, with aircraft parts, automotive suppliers and data centers spread across its industrial parks. The countryside is just as rewarding. East of the city, the wine and cheese route runs through Tequisquiapan and Ezequiel Montes, and the giant monolith of Peña de Bernal rises over the fields. San Miguel de Allende is about an hour away by road.
why_title: Why fly a private jet to Querétaro

why.d: The drive from Mexico City to Querétaro on Highway 57 can take two and a half to three hours with trucks and roadworks. A private jet to Querétaro covers it in about 35 minutes of flight, which turns a lost day on the road into a morning trip.

Fly in with engineers, auditors or a client delegation, tour the plant and be back in Toluca by mid-afternoon. Querétaro Intercontinental sits on the eastern side of the city, close to several of its main industrial and aerospace parks.

The same airport puts you 40 to 50 minutes from Tequisquiapan, Peña de Bernal and the vineyards of Ezequiel Montes, and around an hour and fifteen from San Miguel de Allende. For a wine weekend, the flight is the shortest part of the trip.

Flights start at $3,000 USD one way, per aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. The quote comes back confirmed in 30 minutes on WhatsApp, and domestic flights can be ready about 2 hours after you say yes.

journey_title: A Querétaro morning, door to door

journey.d: Your driver heads west to Toluca on the México-Toluca highway, about an hour at this time of day. Use the ride for calls you would otherwise make from the highway north. An official photo ID is all you need on this domestic flight.

The car pulls up at the private terminal (FBO) at Toluca International. A quick ID check, your bags go aboard, and you are at the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes from the curb. The flight north is shorter than most morning commutes.

Coffee is poured as you climb out of the Valley of Toluca. The flight lasts about as long as a drive from Polanco to Santa Fe in good traffic, and the descent begins before you have finished reading the first file.

You touch down at Querétaro Intercontinental after about 35 minutes. The state shares Mexico City's time zone. Your car is waiting on the private aviation side, and the high-plateau morning air is still cool and clear.

The main industrial parks are 15 to 30 minutes from the airport and the historic center about 30. Run your meetings, have lunch in a courtyard restaurant near the Plaza de Armas, and fly home in the afternoon.

places_title: What to see in Querétaro after you land

places.name: Querétaro Aqueduct
places.d: Built between 1726 and 1735, the aqueduct carried spring water into the city on 74 stone arches. The best view is from the Mirador de los Arcos at the top of Calle Ejército Republicano, especially after dark, when the arches are lit and the city spreads out below.

places.name: Peña de Bernal
places.d: One of the tallest monoliths in the world, a sheer rock tower above the Pueblo Mágico of Bernal, about 50 minutes from the airport. Climb partway up the trail for the view, eat gorditas de maíz quebrado in the village, then taste local wines at the vineyards nearby.

places.name: San Miguel de Allende
places.d: About an hour and fifteen from the airport, this hillside town in Guanajuato is famous for the pink neo-gothic spires of the Parroquia de San Miguel Arcángel, its rooftop bars and its galleries. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most loved small towns in Mexico.

places.name: Tequisquiapan
places.d: A relaxed colonial town at the center of the Querétaro wine and cheese route, about 40 minutes from the airport. Walk its plaza and market, then visit the surrounding vineyards, sparkling-wine cellars and cheese makers around Ezequiel Montes for an afternoon of tastings.

best_time_title: Best time to fly to Querétaro
best_time: Querétaro sits on the high plateau at about 1,800 meters, so days are warm and nights are cool for most of the year. October to May is the dry season, with clear skies that suit both business trips and weekends in wine country. April and May are the warmest months. From June to September afternoon showers are common, and this is also harvest time, when the vineyards around Tequisquiapan and Ezequiel Montes hold their grape-harvest festivals. Business travel runs all year, and a private jet to Querétaro is easy to arrange on short notice, with domestic flights ready about 2 hours after confirmation.
airport: Querétaro Intercontinental Airport (QRO) is about 220 km from Toluca and sits east of the city in the municipality of Colón, next to the state's aerospace park. Private aircraft use the general aviation area, apart from the commercial terminal, and your car can meet you there. The historic center is about 30 minutes away by car, the main industrial parks 15 to 30, Tequisquiapan around 40, Peña de Bernal about 50 and San Miguel de Allende about 1 hour 15 minutes. This is a domestic flight, so there is no customs.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Querétaro
docs: Your flight to Querétaro is domestic, so Mexican nationals only need a valid official photo ID, such as an INE card or a passport. Foreign visitors should carry the passport they used to enter Mexico. Send the full name of every passenger on WhatsApp when you confirm, and the aircraft can be ready about 2 hours later. Customs and immigration do not apply on this route.
